title: Super Ugly Number
hints: this is the same shape of problem as generating ugly numbers with primes 2, 3, 5, just generalized to any given list of primes
every super ugly number besides 1 is some smaller super ugly number multiplied by one of the given primes
use a min-heap seeded with 1. repeatedly pop the smallest value, and for each prime in the list, push value * prime, skipping duplicates you've already generated

the nth distinct value popped is your answer - watch out that with many primes, duplicate products (like 2*7 and 7*2, or 2*13 vs other combinations landing on the same number) are common and must be deduplicated, e.g. with a seen set
commonMistakes: not deduplicating across different prime multiplications that land on the same product, over-counting the sequence
iterating primes with a naive nested loop per candidate integer instead of a heap, which is far slower for large n
forgetting that primes may not be sorted in the input and not needing them to be, since the heap handles ordering regardless

content.problemStatement:
A super ugly number is a positive integer whose only prime factors come from a given list of primes. You're given a number `n` and a list `primes`.

**Return the `n`th super ugly number in ascending order.**

Numbering is 1-indexed, so n = 1 returns the smallest super ugly number. 1 counts as super ugly, since it has no prime factors at all.
constraints: every value in primes is a prime number
notes: a single prime in the primes list, producing only its powers
primes list containing a large prime, creating big gaps in the sequence
